system.summary: One-part numerical code, five-digit groups, alphabetical order (number = page x 100 + line): the Red Code of 1876; a five-letter date-time word opens or closes the groups.

prior_solution.where: The clerk's typed clear texts of K1, K2, K4 and K5 are filed with the cipher telegrams (M367 roll 70, 763.72/8789a, 8790, 8802). No edition, key or study of the telegrams found: nothing in this repository on main (catalogue.json, research/leads.json, targets, 12 Nov 2026), nothing in FRUS 1918; Weber 1979 not consulted. The same 1876 Red Cipher is the key of roosevelt1903 in this repository (William Echols, issue #353, 9 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol written before any calculation). AI agents swept M367 for ciphered files, transcribed, aligned the groups with the clear texts, identified the code and tested its order. No human palaeographer checked the digits.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: OCR sweep of M367 rolls 80-88 (7 371 images) found the five telegrams; clear texts found on roll 70.
The five telegrams transcribed group by group (transcription.txt); clear texts typed from the clerk's sheets (decryption.txt).
69 groups lined up with the words of the period clear texts (key.tsv); date-time words decoded by their scheme.
Order test of a one-part code: concordance 0.9996 over 69 pairs against 0.597 for 200 permutations; two independent values printed by Weber match.
Red Code / Haswell 1876 identified from the clerk's annotations; the codebook (NARA T1171, catalog id 417267710, used for roosevelt1903) not consulted; Weber 1979 not consulted.

Integration check of PR #561: the five telegrams compared with the NARA images (roll 80 0619, 0621; roll 81 0704-0706): 128 groups, six of K5 misread or doubtful, two doubtful in K2; the Red codebook (NARA T1171 roll 1, catalog id 417267710) found online and 23 groups looked up (codebook_check.tsv): all checked values agree, 7 open groups given values, the doubtful digits decided; order test on the corrected 76 values: concordance 1.000 against best 0.598 of 200 shuffles.

K3 'lilum eo' tried with the codebook's spelling code, division 1, key = first number group 25131 (the rule that reads roosevelt1903's KIEL): L I L U = T H Y S; M and 'eo' give no letters of the name in division 1; divisions 2-3 not tried.

Edition check (from roosevelt1903, 14 Nov 2026): the numbered pages of T1171 roll 1 used here belong to the second book on the roll, 'The Cipher of the Department of State' (Government Printing Office, 1876, title page image 0090; slip 'Red Cipher of 1876', image 0094), not to the 1867 book that the roll's NARA target sheet names. Red Code of 1876 confirmed.

outcome.method_basis: The Department's copies are marked 'Red'; the Red codebook of 1876 (NARA T1171, online) gives every group checked and reads K3 in part with its spelling table; four of the five telegrams also have the clerks' clear texts (the contributor's route: 69 values read off them, 'key recovered based on adjacent plaintext').

validation.notes: Order test (structure of the code), not a held-out reading; four labels adjusted after the first pass, declared.

outcome.fraction_read_source: Integration check 14 Nov 2026: 111 tokens, 109 read (K3's 'lilum', read in part as THYS..., and 'eo' are holes); K1, K2, K4, K5 complete.

texts.label: K1 to K5, Department - Kobe, 30 Jan - 9 Feb 1918
texts.summary: The Department asks the Kobe consul to have the Japan Chronicle name the source of a Thyssen article; the Chronicle copied it from a Hong Kong paper, which had it from the Glasgow Post.

reading_review.note: read against the clerk's clear texts; K3 partial; digits not re-checked at full resolution

outcome.notes: No image is reproduced (NARA public domain, but kept out of the repository). The reading is existing; the new things are the find, the identification of the Red Code and the 69 values.
